Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X .

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

 

This is a fully remote position and we're considering candidates in Spain.

About Product Management

As a Product Manager at Grafana Labs, you'll develop a vision and strategy for your product domain. You will own the experience for your product as well as its roadmap and competitive positioning, and you will collaborate with company leadership on setting your product's goals. You will be the primary advocate and expert in your area, with a strong ability to communicate needs, functionality, and details effectively both to external customers and internal stakeholders. The teams and people you will be interacting with will be 100% remote and globally distributed, so strong and proactive communication is essential.

Product Managers are the bridge that connects R&D to GTM. You are a facilitator who ensures the free flow of information across these teams and are expected to be technically proficient when representing our products to our customers.

The role

As the Staff Product Manager for Enterprise Deployment Solutions, you'll own the Grafana Labs offerings that run outside our standard multi-tenant SaaS. That includes Grafana Federal Cloud , for organizations that need FedRAMP-authorized observability: US federal agencies; state, local, and education (SLED) customers; and commercial companies that sell FedRAMP offerings of their own. It also includes Grafana Cloud Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC) , which delivers the full Grafana Cloud experience while the customer pays the infrastructure bill directly to their cloud provider, saving them significantly at scale.

Your mission is to make Grafana Labs the obvious choice for organizations that can't use standard SaaS because of compliance, data, or cost-at-scale constraints. Deployment choices change the product: features that are simple in standard SaaS can be hard, expensive, or impossible in a regulated or customer-owned environment. You’ll be responsible for adapting existing Grafana Cloud capabilities to these environments, deciding which features come in, which wait, and which stay out, and occasionally building something specific to BYOC or Federal Cloud. You'll also help shape which deployment models we offer next.

Along the way, you’ll use AI tools daily to speed up research, analyze product signals, and develop positioning, applying strong judgment to the results.

As the Staff Product Manager for Enterprise Deployment Solutions, you will: 

• Define the vision, strategy, and roadmap for the Grafana Bring Your Own Cloud and Grafana Federal Cloud products, using product data and market research to balance customer value

title: Data Scientist, Cloud Distribution & Growth
description:
About the Team

Cloud service providers give developers a way to use OpenAI models in the environments where they already build and run software. Our team works with Go-to-Market (GTM), Product, Engineering, and Finance to understand which customers we can reach through these providers and what helps them grow from a first API call to a production workload.

About the Role

In your first few months, you’ll identify a customer segment or workload where OpenAI can grow, recommend an investment to GTM, Product, and Engineering, and define how we’ll know whether it brought new usage to OpenAI. Your first priority will be to explain what drives usage and revenue across providers. You’ll use that understanding to help GTM decide which customers and workloads to invest in and to build forecasts the team can plan against.

A customer might sign a substantial cloud commitment and send very little traffic. You can sit down with the account team, trace the customer’s first requests, and work out whether they need help launching, access to a different model, or more capacity. When you see the same opportunity across customers, your work can change where OpenAI invests.

In This Role, You Will:

- Build a reliable view of the business from provider usage reports, billing records, and API logs. Show how new workloads, expansion, changes in price, and shifts in model mix contribute to growth.

- Estimate how much demand cloud distribution adds to OpenAI. Trace customer activity across channels to distinguish new use cases from traffic that moved from the direct API.

- Identify where customers are ready to scale. Combine what account teams hear with evidence on request failures, latency, and model availability. Work with Product and Engineering on a change and measure what happens to usage.

- Shape growth plans with GTM and Finance. Estimate what existing workloads and upcoming launches can contribute by year end, test the assumptions that matter most, and recommend where to focus with each provider.

- Own the consumption forecast. Compare forecasts with actual usage over the same period, explain the biggest misses, and use what you learn to improve the next forecast.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You:

- Like questions that take you from a conversation with an account team to a query about a single API request. You’re curious about why a customer’s behavior differs from what the numbers first suggest.

- Are comfortable making a recommendation while some questions are still open. You can tell a sales leader where you’d invest and explain to an engineer what evidence would change your mind.

Qualifications

- Experience independently leading data science work on a product, growth, or commercial question that changed a business decision.

- Strong SQL and Python skills. You can join incomplete datasets, choose the right unit of analysis, and validate an aggregate result against individual customers or workloads.

- Experience using cohorts, experiments, or observational comparisons to assess what drove a change. You can explain how customer selection affects the conclusion and evaluate a forecast against a simple baseline.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with API platforms, cloud marketplaces, enterprise GTM, or a usage-based business.

- Experience connecting service reliability or capacity to customer adoption, or using demand forecasts to guide a commercial or infrastructure investment.

We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

title: Business Development Representative
description:
ABOUT US

Lorikeet is redefining what customer support looks like - and we're just getting started.

We build AI that handles complex, high-volume support for fintechs, healthtechs, marketplaces, and delivery services. Not chatbot-tier AI. The kind that actually resolves tickets, gives support teams their time back, and raises the bar for what software can do.

We're backed by over $50M USD from QED, Blackbird, and Square Peg, with backing from operators like Claire Hughes Johnson (ex-Stripe COO) and Cristina Cordova (Linear COO), plus founders of Canva, Atlassian, and Airwallex. We're the first company since Canva to be funded at early stage by all three of Australia's top VC funds - which tells you something about the calibre of people who've looked closely at what we're building and said yes.

Our customers include some of the largest telehealth, fintech, and marketplace companies in the US and Australia - many handling over a million support tickets a year. The problems are real, the scale is real, and the work matters.

If you want to build something that genuinely changes how businesses and customers interact - this is the place.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re hiring our founding Business Development Representatives. Today, pipeline at Lorikeet comes from founders, AEs, and a growing demand gen engine. This role exists to add a focused, outbound-first motion on top of that, and you’ll take on far more than a typical BDR seat: building the team, the process, the structure, and the program for the BDRs who come after you. It’s a high-visibility role with real room to grow, into an Account Executive seat, our deployment team, or other roles across the company.

The people you’ll be reaching out to run support for regulated, high-stakes businesses: a telehealth company where a wrong answer is a compliance problem, a fintech where a support ticket can mean someone’s money is stuck. They’ve usually been burned by a chatbot before. Your job isn’t to blast them with sequences, it’s to understand their support operation well enough to show them, specifically, why this time is different, and to earn the first conversation.

You’ll work hand-in-hand with our AEs, founders, and GTM Engineer, and you’ll have a direct line to product. We’re AI-native as a company, and that goes double for how we prospect: you’ll be expected to build and use your own AI tooling, not just run someone else’s cadence.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

- Generate qualified pipeline for our AE team across mid-market and enterprise accounts in fintech, healthtech, marketplaces, and delivery

- Research target accounts deeply, from ticket volumes, channels, regulatory constraints, how their current support experience actually works - and turn that into a sharp, personal reason to talk

- Run multi-threaded outbound across email, phone, and LinkedIn to Heads of Support, CX, and Operations, and the executives above them

- Test-drive prospects’ existing support experiences and bring what you find into your outreach (it’s one of the most effective openers we have)

- Follow up fast on inbound, events, and campaigns, partnering with Demand Gen so nothing warm goes cold

- Build and iterate on your own AI-powered prospecting workflows with Claude Code and our GTM Engineer - research agents, account scoring, personalised messaging at scale

- Qualify rigorously and hand off cleanly, so AEs walk into first calls already knowing the account

- Feed what you hear from the market back to sales, marketing, and product - objections, competitor mentions, and the problems buyers actually care about

- Own your territory and account plans: decide where to focus, build engagement plans for key accounts, and prepare thoroughly before every outreach

- Build the BDR function from the ground up: the playbook, what we measure, which plays work, and how we hire and onboard the next BDRs

THE RIGHT CANDIDATE WILL HAVE:

- 1-3 years of experience in a BDR/SDR or other customer-facing, target-carrying role

title: Supervisor, Revenue Recovery Support
description:
EnableComp provides Specialty Revenue Cycle Management solutions for healthcare organizations, leveraging over 24 years of industry-leading expertise and its unified E360 RCM ™ intelligent automation platform to improve financial sustainability for hospitals, health systems, and ambulatory surgery centers (ASCs) nationwide. Powered by proprietary algorithms, iterative intelligence from 10M+ processed claims, and expert human-in-the-loop integration, EnableComp provides solutions across the revenue lifecycle for Veterans Administration, Workers’ Compensation, Motor Vehicle Accidents, and Out-of-State Medicaid claims as well as denials for all payer classes. By partnering with clients to supercharge the reimbursement process, EnableComp removes the burden of payment from patients and provider organizations while enabling accelerated cash, higher and more accurate yield, clean AR management, reduced denials, and data-rich performance management. EnableComp is a multi-year recipient the Top Workplaces award and was recognized as Black Book's #1 Specialty Revenue Cycle Management Solution provider in 2024 and is among the top one percent of companies to make the Inc. 5000 list of the fastest-growing private companies in the United States for the last eleven years.

Position Summary:

The Supervisor, Revenue Recovery Support provides daily leadership to Revenue Recovery Support Specialists and Revenue Specialists. This role coordinates client support, payment and system review, account follow-up for medical necessity, DRG validation, and Zero Balance accounts. The Supervisor sets daily priorities, monitors quality and inventory, resolves escalated issues, and coaches team members to ensure accurate, timely work.

Key Responsibilities:

• Supervise assigned team members, distribute work, and monitor productivity, quality, inventory, and turnaround times.

• Train and coach employees, provide regular feedback, complete performance evaluations, and address performance concerns in partnership with department leadership.

• Participate in hiring, onboarding, scheduling, and other employee life cycle activities.

• Coordinate timely, accurate responses to client requests and keep management informed of significant or recurring issues.

• Review client systems and payment activity to identify account placement or payment discrepancies, process gaps, and potential revenue opportunities.

• Direct and support follow-up on medical necessity, DRG validation, and Zero Balance accounts, ensuring that research, payer contact, and account documentation are completed appropriately.

• Prioritize accounts based on financial opportunity, aging, payer requirements, timely filing, and client expectations.

• Conduct quality reviews and address gaps in account research, documentation, follow-up, and client communication.

• Review team reports and performance measures; share inventory risks, trends, and recommended actions with management.

• Partner with Revenue Recovery, Client Success, Data Quality, Product, Technology, and other teams to resolve issues affecting client support or account resolution.

• Maintain working knowledge of payer policies, medical necessity requirements, DRG reimbursement concepts, billing practices, and client workflows.

• Ensure team activities follow client requirements, internal procedures, and privacy and security standards.

• Identify opportunities to improve team workflows, training, and documentation, and support approved changes.

• Perform other duties as required.

Requirements and Qualifications:

• High school diploma or GED required; associate or bachelor’s degree preferred. An equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.

• 4+ years of experience in healthcare billing, collections, revenue cycle operations, or revenue recovery.

title: Restaurant Partnership Manager - North
description:
About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we’re building the delivery of (almost) everything and you’ll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn’t always easy, but it’s definitely exciting. Here you’ll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You’ll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you’re a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

Wolt is a technology company known for our delivery platform that connects people with the best restaurants and retailers in their city. But we’re so much more than that. We’re building an ecosystem that helps restaurants thrive, supports local businesses and communities, and brings great food to people’s doorsteps. Our restaurant team plays a vital role in expanding Wolt’s presence across different regions, with a strong focus on building meaningful relationships with partners and ensuring operational excellence.

We are now looking for a Restaurant Partnership Manager to join our team and support our rapidly growing restaurant business in Northern Israel , one of our largest and most strategically important regions.

If you are passionate about local commerce and the restaurant industry, have a strong commercial mindset, enjoy building things from the ground up, and thrive in a dynamic, hands-on environment, we’d love to hear from you!

What you’ll be doing

As a Restaurant Partnership Manager, you’ll play a key role in ensuring new Resturant partners are successfully onboarded and supported throughout their early days on the platform. You will act as the bridge between our Resturant Development and Platform teams, making sure every detail is in place before and after the onboarding of partners or area launches.

Day-to-day in this role you’ll:

• Identify potential new partners or opportunities in the area that fit Wolt’s Restaurant strategy.

• Act as the main point of contact for Restaurants partners in the northern areas during onboarding and the launch of new areas.

• Support the Sales Team with field-related activities and assist with daily operational tasks & launching new products.

• Prepare stores for go-live by coordinating with multiple stakeholders and ensuring all operational elements are in place.

• Review and update menu item lists and product data to ensure accuracy and relevance on the Wolt platform.

• Coordinate the exchange of documentation with partners, ensuring all information is well-organized and compliant.

•  Contribute to improving and streamlining our sales and onboarding processes by sharing insights from the field.

Our humble expectations* 

We’re looking for someone experienced, proactive, and ready to take ownership of their work in a growing and evolving team. If you’re passionate about Restaurants, love working with people, and want to be part of something dynamic, this role might be a great fit.

•  4-6 years of relevant experience in sales management roles, account management, field operations, or sales support.

• Based in the north of Israel, this is an almost fully local, field-focused role, so proximity to the region is a significant advantage.

• Excellent interpersonal and communication skills - you know how to adjust your tone based on the audience.

• Strong attention to detail, structured approach to work, and ability to manage multiple tasks at once.

• Tech-savvy and comfortable working with digital tools and systems.

• Independent and solution-oriented, with the drive to improve processes and make things better.

• Fluent in Hebrew and English

• Valid driver’s license - this role includes regular field work in the northern areas

Powered by world-class technology and a user-first mindset, Bybit delivers a seamless ecosystem across trading, payments, wealth management, custody, institutional services, and Web3 - connecting users to the future of digital finance.

- Du verantwortest deinen eigenen Funnel vom Erstkontakt bis zum Abschluss.

- Deine Woche planst du eigenverantwortlich, mit klaren Zielen und einer Führungskraft, die dich unterstützt und weiterentwickelt.

- Du gibst dein Wissen weiter - im Roleplay, im Shadowing und im Austausch mit Kolleg:innen, die neu dabei sind.

DAS BRINGST DU MIT

- Nachweisbare Erfahrung im B2B-Vertrieb mit eigener Abschlussverantwortung über den gesamten Sales-Cycle hinweg, von der Kaltakquise bis zum Closing.

- Hohe Selbststeuerung und Eigenverantwortung - du gehörst zu den ersten Teammitgliedern vor Ort.

- Du bist es gewohnt, an KPIs gemessen zu werden und hast deine eigenen Zahlen stets im Blick.

- Du schaffst es, ein komplexes Produkt verständlich zu vermitteln und dabei zu begeistern.

- Du bist lernbereit, setzt Feedback um und willst dich weiterentwickeln.

- Du bist sicher im Umgang mit digitalen Tools.

- Verhandlungssicheres bis muttersprachliches Deutsch sowie gute Englischkenntnisse.

- Führerschein der Klasse B und Freude daran, in deiner Region unterwegs zu sein.

DAS ERWARTET DICH BEI UNS

- Klare Entwicklungschancen: Nächste Senioritätsstufen erreichst du mit deiner Performance - simpel gehalten und schnell erreichbar. Außerdem besetzen wir Team-Lead-Rollen bevorzugt aus dem eigenen Team und begleiten den Weg dorthin mit unserer Sales Manager Academy.

- Eine Führungskraft und Kolleg:innen, die dich jederzeit unterstützen.

- Strukturierte Einarbeitung und praxisnahe Begleitung über die ersten Monate hinweg (Ramp-Up Programm).

- Klare KPIs & Performance-Transparenz, damit du jederzeit weißt, wo du stehst.

- Eigenverantwortliche Wochenplanung und Vertrauensarbeitszeit.

- Firmenwagen inkl. Tankkarte sowie MacBook und iPhone.

- 50 € steuerfreies Guthaben pro Monat über Probonio.

- Fixgehalt und ungedeckelte Provision.

- Teamevents, die ihren Namen verdienen: Sommerfest, Winterfeier und regelmäßige Teamformate.

WIE GEHT ES WEITER?

1. Bewerbung & Sichtung - wir melden uns so schnell wie möglich bei dir.

2. Erstgespräch mit unserem Recruiting-Team (ca. 30-45 Minuten).

3. Video-Call mit deiner künftigen Führungskraft.

4. Field Day - zwei Stunden bei uns im Office. Du siehst, wie wir arbeiten, wir sehen dich in Aktion.

5. Abschlussgespräch mit unserer Head of Sales.

Salonkee steht für Chancengleichheit und Vielfalt. Wir freuen uns über Bewerbungen von Menschen mit unterschiedlichen Hintergründen, Perspektiven und Fähigkeiten - unabhängig von Geschlecht, Herkunft, Alter, Behinderung, Religion oder Identität.

title: Planning Manager
description:
Position Summary:
The Planning Manager is a leadership role responsible for the overall strategy, direction, and execution of the inventory planning function across all stocked product categories, including Wallcovering, Fabric, Furnishings, and carpet. This role is accountable for leading the team, developing world-class demand forecasts, optimizing inventory investment and ensuring product availability to support sales growth and maximize working capital efficiency. The Manager drives continuous improvement in planning processes and tools, manages key vendor relationships strategically, and serves as the primary liaison between Planning and senior leadership from Procurement, Category Management Team (CMT), Sales, and Operations. Expect high-level strategic thinking, decisive team leadership, and ultimate accountability for overall inventory health.
Key Responsibilities:
Team Leadership & Development

• Lead, mentor, and develop a team of Inventory Planners and Senior Planners.

• Set team strategy, goals, and priorities, and monitor progress toward overall inventory objectives.

• Oversee performance management, coaching, and training of team members, fostering a culture of high performance and accuracy.

• Responsible for distributing information to the team from upper management.

Inventory Strategy & Demand Planning

• Responsible for setting and maintaining the overall inventory investment strategy across all assigned product categories.

• Direct the development of robust, rolling demand forecasts using advanced historical sales data (30/60/90-day trends), seasonal patterns, and project pipeline inputs.

• Establish, audit, and maintain core inventory parameters (reorder points, safety stock) across the team to minimize risk and optimize working capital.

• Proactively monitor and manage inventory health metrics, including aged inventory exposure, stockout risks, and overstock situations.

Supply Chain & Vendor Management

• Oversee the strategic partnership with key wallcovering, fabric, and furnishing vendors to secure supply and negotiate optimal production schedules and order quantities.

• Lead the coordination with Purchasing teams to determine buy quantities, replenishment timing, and mitigate high-risk supply disruptions.

• Directly manage the review of supplier performance for delivery and service level, implementing necessary improvement plans.

• Manage inventory exposure across key mills and suppliers.

Reporting, Analysis & Process Improvement

• Design, develop, and maintain advanced inventory performance dashboards and weekly health reports for senior leadership.

• Oversee the monitoring of forecast accuracy and bias across the team, implementing corrective actions to forecasting models and planning tools.

• Identify, champion, and implement strategic improvements to planning tools, processes, and reporting capabilities across the organization.

Cross-Functional Leadership

• Serve as the primary inventory planning partner to the Category Management Team (CMT) to align buying strategies and uphold product & vendor goals.

• Partner with sales teams to incorporate customer demand insights and upcoming project requirements.

• Collaborate with warehouse and operations teams to manage stock allocation and replenishment, including coordinating transport of goods.

QUI SOMMES-NOUS ?

Premier groupe public de grandes écoles d’ingénieurs et de management en France, l’Institut Mines-Télécom (IMT) est un acteur majeur de l’enseignement supérieur, de la recherche et de l’innovation au service du développement économique, industriel et technologique de la France.
Héritier de plus de deux siècles d’histoire scientifique, technologique et industrielle, il fédère huit grandes écoles publiques - IMT Atlantique, IMT Mines Albi, IMT Mines Alès, IMT Nord Europe, Institut Mines-Télécom Business School, Mines Saint-Étienne, Télécom Paris et Télécom SudParis - et deux écoles filiales, EURECOM et InSIC.

title: CMC & Manufacturing Lead, Life Sciences
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic’s Life Sciences team is working to make Claude a useful partner across biology and drug development, so that promising science can reach patients sooner. Genetic medicines are one area where we see real potential, particularly for diseases with few or no treatment options.

Chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC) often sets the pace in this field. We’re hiring a CMC & Manufacturing Lead to bring deep technical expertise to our team. You’ll guide CMC strategy across a range of genetic medicine technologies, work closely with external partners, and help our researchers and engineers make Claude useful for real CMC work.

Much of today’s CMC practice was built for products made at scale for large populations. You’ll help work out what better approaches could look like for smaller ones, including platform processes, faster testing, and ways to carry knowledge from one product to the next.

If you have deep experience manufacturing genetic medicines and want to explore how AI can help accelerate the way they’re developed, we’d love to hear from you.

Key responsibilities

• Guide CMC and manufacturing strategy for genetic medicines, from early development through clinical supply

• Serve as a CMC expert to external partners, reviewing process, analytical, and supply plans and resolving technical issues together

• Provide technical oversight of externally conducted process development, formulation, analytical development, fill-finish, stability, and release testing, with phase-appropriate specifications and control strategies

• Collaborate with scientists across disciplines to turn early research into robust, GMP-ready processes

• Oversee quality for externally manufactured material, including audits, quality agreements, and batch disposition

• Evaluate novel manufacturing, analytical, and delivery technologies, and make clear recommendations

• Develop approaches that reduce the time and cost of reaching clinical material without compromising product quality or patient safety

• Work with Anthropic researchers and engineers to identify where Claude can speed up CMC work, contribute to evaluations and tools, and test results against real-world problems

• Identify CMC and supply chain risks early, and communicate status, tradeoffs, and decisions clearly

Minimum qualifications

• Biotechnology or pharmaceutical industry experience leading CMC for gene therapy, gene editing, or nucleic acid products, including taking a product from preclinical development into the clinic

• Deep expertise in several of the following, and working knowledge of the others: lipid nanoparticles (LNP), mRNA, guide RNA (gRNA), adeno-associated virus (AAV), and antisense oligonucleotides (ASO), including how they are manufactured, characterized, and released

• Deep understanding of GMP manufacturing and regulatory CMC requirements for genetic medicines, including writing or reviewing CMC sections of INDs or equivalent filings

• A strong track record of selecting and managing CDMOs, CROs, and other external partners, including technology transfer and quality oversight

• Demonstrated creativity in manufacturing novel products, shown by process, analytical, or supply solutions you developed where no established precedent existed

• Ability to evaluate novel technologies rigorously from data and turn that evaluation into a clear recommendation

• Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining CMC tradeoffs to people outside the field

• Curiosity about how AI can change drug development, and excitement about Anthropic’s mission to build safe and beneficial AI
